_note: QM #156 (c): place-specific notes for AOV town pages whose published data is too thin to tell them apart. Plain facts about council, setting and building stock; no invented statistics.
antrim: Antrim sits on the north-east shore of Lough Neagh and is run by Antrim and Newtownabbey Borough Council. The buildings that carry smoke vents here are mostly apartment schemes near the town centre and Junction One, care settings, and industrial units on the roads out toward Belfast International Airport. A lot of the residential stock is two- and three-storey walk-up flats, where the vent is a single head-of-stair window actuator rather than a shaft system. When you send details, tell us whether the building control approval came through the council or was part of a Housing Executive scheme, because that decides which fire strategy we work from.
armagh: Armagh is a cathedral city in Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough, with a Georgian core around the Mall and newer estates on the edges. Listed and conservation-area buildings change what can be fitted: a replacement vent on a stair in the historic centre often has to keep the existing frame and glazing pattern, so the actuator and control panel do most of the work. Student and shared housing near the Mall and purpose-built apartments on the ring roads are the usual jobs. Photos of the window and the panel label let us check parts before anyone travels.
ballymena: Ballymena is the main town of Mid and East Antrim Borough, with a busy retail centre and manufacturing on the edge of town. Smoke ventilation work here is split between mixed-use buildings over shops on the main streets, newer apartment blocks, and natural smoke and heat exhaust on industrial roofs. Industrial roof vents use different actuators and controls from a domestic stair vent, so tell us which you have. Where a building has been converted from offices to flats, check whether the original vent was ever commissioned for the new layout; we see that gap often in converted town-centre stock.
banbridge: Banbridge sits on the River Bann in Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough, best known for its cut on the main street where the road runs under an overpass. The building stock is mostly low-rise, with apartment schemes added around the town centre and near the A1 junctions. Most smoke vent calls are for one or two stair cores with a single panel. If the panel is a basic single-zone unit, a fault is often a failed actuator or a flat standby battery, both of which we can confirm from photos before a visit.
bangor-northern-ireland: Bangor is the largest town in Ards and North Down Borough, on the southern shore of Belfast Lough with a large marina. Seafront apartments and retirement developments along the coast make up much of the smoke ventilation work, and salt air shortens the life of exposed actuators and roof vent hinges. We check corrosion on the vent frame as well as the electrical side. For blocks with a managing agent, send the last service sheet so we can see whether the vent has been tested to the full open position or only cycled at the panel.
belfast: Belfast is the largest city in Northern Ireland and has by far the widest range of smoke control: purpose-built student blocks around Queen's and Ulster University, Titanic Quarter and city-centre apartments, offices with mechanical smoke extract, and older converted buildings. Mechanical systems with fans, dampers and a fire-fighting interface need a different visit from a single stair vent, so tell us which you have and roughly how many floors. Belfast City Council handles building control, and the fire strategy for a newer block will usually name the system type we need to test against.
carrickfergus: Carrickfergus sits on the north shore of Belfast Lough in Mid and East Antrim Borough, with its Norman castle by the harbour. Harbourside apartments and sheltered housing are the main users of automatic vents, and the coastal setting means corrosion on roof vents and window hinges. Many blocks are three or four storeys with one protected stair. If the vent will not close fully after a test, salt build-up on the frame or a worn chain actuator is the usual cause, and both are worth photographing before we quote.
coleraine: Coleraine is on the River Bann in Causeway Coast and Glens Borough and is home to an Ulster University campus. Student accommodation and purpose-built flats near the university and the town centre are typical smoke vent jobs, along with care homes and some industrial units. Student blocks are busy and doors get wedged, so we check that the vent opens when the system says it does, not just that the panel shows healthy. Term-time access is easier to arrange if you tell us the block manager's preferred window.
derry: Derry, on the River Foyle, is the main city of Derry City and Strabane District, with its walled centre and newer development on both banks. Smoke ventilation work covers city-centre apartments, student housing near the Magee campus, hotels and healthcare buildings. Older buildings inside and near the walls are often converted, so the vent may be a later addition with its own small panel. Tell us whether the building is on the Cityside or the Waterside and roughly how old the conversion is; it helps us bring the right actuator range.
dungannon: Dungannon is a market town in Mid Ulster District with a strong manufacturing base around it. Most smoke vent work is on newer apartment schemes in and around the town, on care settings, and on factory and warehouse roofs where natural smoke and heat exhaust ventilators are fitted. Roof vents on industrial buildings have pneumatic or 24 V actuators and are tested differently from a stair window. Tell us the building type and send a photo of the panel; a lot of local units are older systems where parts need checking first.
enniskillen: Enniskillen is the county town of Fermanagh, built on an island between the upper and lower parts of Lough Erne, in Fermanagh and Omagh District. Apartments, hotels and healthcare buildings are the typical smoke vent sites, and much of the town-centre stock is older property with later conversions. Travel from Stockport means we plan Enniskillen visits as a scheduled run, so it helps to group several buildings or tests together. Send the address list and the panel makes and we will quote the run as one visit.
greater-glasgow: Greater Glasgow covers the city and the surrounding built-up area, so smoke ventilation work ranges from tenement conversions to high-rise residential blocks and new build-to-rent schemes. Scottish building standards and the fire strategy for each building set the test, not the English guidance. Many older tenements have a single roof hatch or cupola vent on the common stair, while newer towers use shaft systems with fans. Tell us which you have and the number of storeys, and send the last service sheet if you have one.
larne: Larne is a ferry port town in Mid and East Antrim Borough, at the start of the Causeway Coastal Route. Sheltered housing, apartment blocks near the harbour and town centre, and port and industrial buildings make up the usual work. Exposure to the sea air matters here as it does in Carrickfergus and Bangor: hinges, chains and roof vent seals wear faster. A photo of the vent open and closed is the most useful thing you can send before a quote.
lurgan: Lurgan is in Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough, next to the large Lurgan Park and close to Craigavon. Terraced streets around the centre sit beside apartment schemes, care homes and industrial estates. Smoke vent work tends to be small residential cores and factory roof vents. If you manage both Lurgan and Portadown buildings, we can test them on the same run because the towns are a few miles apart.
newry: Newry is a city on the Newry Canal in Newry, Mourne and Down District, close to the border and on the main Belfast to Dublin corridor. City-centre apartments, retail buildings with flats above, hotels and healthcare sites are the main smoke vent jobs. Cross-border trade means some buildings were fitted with equipment from Irish suppliers, so the panel label is especially useful when you get in touch. We match parts to what is installed rather than swapping systems.
newtownabbey: Newtownabbey is the large urban area north of Belfast in Antrim and Newtownabbey Borough, made up of several former villages along the lough shore and the hills. Housing association apartments, care homes and business park units are typical smoke ventilation sites. Many blocks were built in the same period by the same developers, so if one vent has a recurring fault, a neighbouring block may have the same one. Tell us if you manage a group and we will check them together.
newtownards: Newtownards sits at the head of Strangford Lough in Ards and North Down Borough, below Scrabo Tower. Apartment developments around the town centre and the lough side, sheltered housing and retail buildings are the usual smoke vent sites. Lough-side blocks see wind-driven rain, which can trip rain sensors and close vents unexpectedly, so tell us if the system closes on its own. That points to a sensor or a weather override setting rather than a fire fault.
omagh: Omagh is the county town of Tyrone, in Fermanagh and Omagh District, where the Camowen and Drumragh rivers meet to form the Strule. The hospital and healthcare buildings, apartment blocks near the centre and care homes are the main smoke vent sites. As with Enniskillen, Omagh visits are planned as scheduled runs from Stockport, so grouping tests or repairs into one visit keeps the cost down. Send the panel make and a photo of the vent and we will confirm parts first.
portadown: Portadown is on the River Bann in Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough, a railway junction town with a large retail centre. Apartment schemes, care homes, shops with flats above and industrial units fill most of the smoke ventilation work. Older flats over shops sometimes have a vent added during conversion with no commissioning record, and we can test and document it so the responsible person has a record. Lurgan and Portadown jobs can share a visit.
strabane: Strabane is a border town on the River Mourne in Derry City and Strabane District, facing Lifford across the river. Smoke ventilation work here is mainly social housing apartments, care settings and town-centre buildings with flats over shops. Visits are planned with Derry jobs where possible, since the two are close. If your building has had a recent refurbishment, tell us, because a new fire door layout can change what the vent needs to do.
bexhill: Bexhill-on-Sea is a seaside town in Rother District, East Sussex, with a large retired population and a seafront lined with mansion blocks and modern apartments around the De La Warr Pavilion. Retirement and sheltered housing blocks with lifts and one or two stair cores are the typical smoke vent sites. Sea air shortens the life of roof vents and actuators. Send the managing agent's last service report and a photo of the vent and panel.
broomhall-windlesham-virginia-water: This ONS built-up area covers Broomhall, Windlesham and Virginia Water on the Surrey and Berkshire border, close to Wentworth and the M3 and M25. Much of the housing is detached, so smoke vent work is concentrated in apartment developments, retirement schemes, care homes and office conversions rather than streets of flats. Many developments are gated and managed, so send the managing agent's contact and access details with your enquiry.
bulford-camp: Bulford Camp is a military garrison on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire. Smoke ventilation work here relates to service accommodation blocks, offices and support buildings, where access is controlled and works go through the estate's own approval process. Tell us who the estate manager is and what access clearance is needed; we will not attend without the site's permission and an agreed date.
croesowallt: Croesoswallt is the Welsh name for Oswestry, a market town in Shropshire close to the Welsh border. It is listed under this name in the published towns file. Apartment schemes in and around the town centre, care homes and industrial units on the edge of town are the usual smoke vent jobs. As the town is in England, the English approved documents apply, but buildings managed from Wales sometimes follow Welsh contractor paperwork; tell us which your managing agent expects.
frampton-cotterell-winterbourne: Frampton Cotterell and Winterbourne are neighbouring villages north of Bristol in South Gloucestershire, recorded together as one built-up area. Most homes are houses, so smoke ventilation work is limited to small apartment schemes, retirement housing and care settings. Many are low-rise blocks with one stair and a single window vent. A photo of the vent and the panel is usually enough for us to quote a test or a repair.
wootton-bassett: Royal Wootton Bassett is a market town in Wiltshire, west of Swindon and close to the M4. Newer apartment blocks around the town, retirement housing and business units near the motorway make up most smoke vent work. With Swindon nearby, managing agents often hold buildings in both, and we can plan one run. Send the addresses and panel makes together.
